channel.title: Undra blog
channel.description: Comparisons, architecture and design notes from the Undra team.

item.title: Undra 1.2: no drift between iOS, Android and the web
item.description: One Rust core made three hosts agree on their logic. 1.2 makes them agree on everything else: a command that diffs one flow recorded on each platform, custom ports that compile on iOS on the first try, and a merge gate in half the time.

item.title: A week of outside use: seven findings, five fixes
item.description: A team tried Undra for a week and sent seven findings. Five are fixed, each with a decision record and a review; two were not taken on, and why.

item.title: Fifteen levers: the JavaScript runtime at 16 KB
item.description: How what a hello-world page loads up front of @undra/runtime went from 22,100 to 15,774 bytes gzipped without removing a feature.

item.title: Undra 1.0: one Rust core under native apps
item.description: What Undra is, who it is for, what is in 1.0, how to try it in five minutes, and what it is not.

item.title: Why Undra is the default choice
item.description: A sourced matrix of what KMP, UniFFI, Flutter and React Native stop you doing, what Undra solved and how, what it costs to adopt, and what is still open.

item.title: Reads never cross the boundary: how Undra's state model works
item.description: How Undra mirrors Rust state into SwiftUI, Compose and React: change-sets, keyed lists as recorded operations, a schema-hash gate, and what it all costs.

item.title: Undra vs Kotlin Multiplatform: sharing logic without leaving your platform
item.description: Undra and Kotlin Multiplatform both share logic and keep the UI native. A dated, sourced comparison: iOS, web, reads, tooling, ecosystem and team fit.

item.title: Undra vs UniFFI and Crux: three ways to put Rust under a native app
item.description: Three ways to put a Rust core under SwiftUI, Compose and React: UniFFI bindings, Crux's Elm-style core, and Undra's mirrored state. Dated and sourced.

item.title: Why Undra keeps your UI native
item.description: Shared UI and shared logic are different bets. What Flutter, React Native and Compose Multiplatform trade, who should pick which, and where Undra stops.
